name: Elements Restoration
body:
School transmutation [void]; Level psychic 7, shaman 7, sorcerer/wizard 7, witch 7

Casting Time 1 full-round action

Range touch

Target one touched creature or unattended object

Void: Spells with this descriptor are tied with a philosophical school of magic based on a concept known as the Void. The school teaches that the Void is the nothingness from which springs forth creativity, insight, spirit, thought, and also the source of pure energy from which all elements and phenomena are derived. Channeling the power of the Void (or the Void element) allows for the manipulation of the elements in objects and creatures, among other possibilities. Spells with the void descriptor are considered to belong to the Void element (for geomancers) and the void elemental school (for void elementalists).

If a spell has the [void] descriptor, it cannot be dispelled by elements release regardless of how high is your CL.

This spell breaks down and disperses moderate concentrations of the elements on the target, cleansing to restore it to its natural state. This functions as elements release, except as above and that it affects each on-going 4th level or lower spells (including from spell-like abilities). As part of casting this spell, you may expend 4 ki points to add +2d4 to your CL for the purposes of this spell.

The target is also healed (or repaired if the target is an object) an amount of damage equal to 1d8 for each 1st level or higher spell successfully dispelled by elements restoration, to a maximum of 5d8. This healing is done by the Void as it restores the balance of the elements in the target, thus it cannot harm the target in any way.

Any healing in excess of the target’s maximum hit points is lost instead.
